latin: Dictum illud Zoroastris, ne exeas cum transit Lictor < >, perfecte intelligetur per illud Exodi, quando sunt prohibiti Israhelite exire domos suas in transitu angeli interficientis primogenita aegyptiorum.
latin_note: 1486 reads 'ne ex eas' and 'trasit' for 'ne exeas'/'transit'; the blank space in the editio princeps (apparently left for an Aramaic word) is omitted in 1487 (farmer1998:25017).
translation: That saying of Zoroaster, 'Do not go out when the lictor passes < >,' will be perfectly understood through that passage of Exodus, where the Israelites were forbidden to leave their houses while the angel passed, killing the firstborn of the Egyptians.
translation_note: Sense checked against farmer1998:25001, which renders 'Lictor' as 'the attendant'; 'the lictor' is kept here as the closer equivalent of the Roman office named in the Latin. No divergence in sense.
